Natsuko includes FFmpeg 9.0.1 (https://ffmpeg.org/) and dav1d 1.5.4
(https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d).

FFmpeg copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers.
FFmpeg is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1
or later. This build disables GPL and nonfree components. See
FFmpeg-LGPL-2.1.txt and FFmpeg-LICENSE.md for its license terms.

dav1d copyright (c) 2018-2025, VideoLAN and dav1d authors.
dav1d uses the BSD 2-Clause license; see dav1d-BSD-2-Clause.txt.

LLVM compiler runtime notices are in LLVM-NOTICE.txt.
Android NDK startup/header notices are in Android-NDK-SYSROOT-NOTICE.txt.
Additional source-level copyrights and license terms are retained in
FFmpeg-THIRD-PARTY.txt and dav1d-THIRD-PARTY.txt.

This software is based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.
Natsuko has not modified FFmpeg's IJG-derived jfdctfst.c,
jfdctint_template.c or jrevdct.c files.

The complete unmodified FFmpeg and dav1d source archives, source checksums,
signature verification material and build provenance are distributed with
Natsuko's source under third_party/ffmpeg/. The corresponding build script is
scripts/build-ffmpeg.sh. These executables run as separate child processes; no
FFmpeg library is linked into the application's Kotlin code.

The corresponding native source archive must accompany each Natsuko release
at its download location. It includes both source archives, build scripts,
configuration reports, checksums and notices. See docs/native_licenses.md in
Natsuko's source for rebuilding and replacing the executables. Upstream source
links below identify the originals and do not replace this source delivery.
Natsuko's own Apache 2.0 license does not relicense these dependencies.

Upstream source archives:
https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-9.0.1.tar.xz
https://download.videolan.org/pub/videolan/dav1d/1.5.4/dav1d-1.5.4.tar.xz
